summary: Kuwohi (formerly Clingmans Dome) Observation Tower: a 1959 Mission 66 concrete tower on the Smokies' highest summit, reached by a paved trail.

facts.design: Mission 66 concrete observation tower with a 375-foot ramp

access.note: Open to visitors, who walk a steep paved trail up from the Kuwohi parking area.

visit.trail_note: About a one-mile round trip on a steep, paved trail from the Kuwohi parking area; the ramp rises gradually to the platform.

facts.agency: National Park Service (Great Smoky Mountains National Park)

events.note: A 40-foot observation tower stood on the dome in 1939, according to a newspaper item about a wedding there.
Mission 66 concrete observation tower, designed by Bebb and Olson of Knoxville and built by W.C. Norris Construction.
Rehabilitation of the entry plaza, ramp and platform began in late August 2017 and officially concluded in August 2018; the tower stayed open.

corrections.why: The NPS gives the 1959 tower as 45 feet (13.7 m). The 40-foot (12.2 m) figure matches the 40-foot tower described in the 1939 item.
Spelling: the park is the Great Smoky Mountains National Park, as the NPS page names it.

corrections.proposed: Kuwohi Observation Tower (formerly Clingmans Dome Observation Tower)
corrections.why: The NPS now uses the Kuwohi name for this tower. Editor to decide whether the record name changes.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 12.2 m (40 feet) matches the 40-foot tower of 1939; the 45-foot (13.7 m) tower standing today dates from 1959.

sources.title: Clingmans Dome Restoration: What's it all about?
A Midcentury Observation Tower in the Smokies Gets a Refresh

notes_for_editor: Name changed to Kuwohi per the NPS page; the NPS does not give the renaming date in the page read. The 1958 bid (source 2) and the 1959 completion (source 3) are read as the same tower; sources do not say so in one sentence. The 1939 tower's fate is not in any source read. Road closures (winter, and occasional half-day closures) appeared only in search snippets, not in a read page, so they are not stated. Source 4's 'remained open' sentence is the basis for the access note during repairs, not for today's access.
